LESSON: FRIENDSHIP AND KEEPING PROMISES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Sadachaar (Social Ethics)
Topic 5.1: Friendship and Keeping Promises

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Friendship and Keeping Promises
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How can you stay away from bad influences online?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Skill 1: identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship

Teach
• Today’s focus: identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship.
• Listen/read the idea.
• Watch/study the model.
• Then do Try this.

Worked example
• Model A for “identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship” using a school example.
• Model B for “identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship” using a home/county example.

Try this
• Your turn: show "identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship" in 3 bullet points.
• Share with a partner and improve one bullet.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• Model 1: identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Practise: identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Make a one-page revision sheet for Friendship and Keeping Promises.
2. Teach someone at home for 2 minutes using bullet points only.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you stay away from bad influences online?
2. Why is it important to consider safety measures while chatting online with friends?
3. What are the ways of developing friendship with Paramatma?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• identify the qualities of a good friendship for a healthy social relationship

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
